samples.summary: `isCellTable`/`toCellPatch` call string methods on values the JSON import path never coerces to strings, breaking `sheets import` of an array-of-arrays JSON containing numbers
samples.evidence: `sheets-import.ts:66` does `rows = parsed as string[][]` — an *unchecked cast*; a JSON file like `[[1,2],[3,4]]` yields numbers at runtime. The new code then calls `data[0].map((h) => h.trim().toLowerCase())` (`csv-parse.ts:105`) and `text.startsWith('=')` (`csv-parse.ts:91`), both of which throw `TypeError: h.trim is not a function` / `text.startsWith is not a function`. The previous `buildCellMap` only did `value === ''` and `cells[ref] = { value }`, so numeric JSON imported fine. The throw is swallowed by the surrounding try/catch into an `outputError` envelope, so the whole import now fails with a confusing message where it previously succeeded.

samples.summary: Round-tripping a default (non-`--raw`) CSV export writes the neutralizing `'` prefix into the destination's *formula* field, silently corrupting formulas
samples.evidence: `buildCellMapFromTable` sends `{ formula }` verbatim whenever the formula column is non-empty (line 126-127). A default export neutralizes that column to `'=SUM(B2:B100)` (`csv.ts:41`). Importing that file therefore PATCHes the cell with `f: "'=SUM(B2:B100)"` — a malformed formula stored server-side, with no error and `imported: N` reported as success. Only the docs warn to pass `--raw`; nothing in the import path detects the guard prefix or rejects it.

samples.summary: `buildCellMap` now reinterprets any grid-CSV cell whose text starts with `=` as a formula, changing existing import semantics and breaking export→import identity for literal `=`-leading text
samples.evidence: `toCellPatch(text)` returns `{ formula: text }` for anything starting with `=` and is now used by `buildCellMap` (line 149), which previously always produced `{ value }`. A cell legitimately set as text (`cells set A1 "=N/A"` stores `v='=N/A'`) exports with `value='=N/A'`, and `buildCellMapFromTable` line 129 routes it through `toCellPatch`, so the re-import converts stored text into an evaluated formula. Existing CSVs containing `=`-leading text columns silently change meaning on import.

samples.summary: `cells batch --dry-run` now bypasses `parseOutputFormat` and runs `getConfig`/`printDryRun` outside any try/catch
samples.evidence: The dry-run block was hoisted out of the try at lines 147-155; `parseOutputFormat(opts.format)` is only reached in the second try at line 158. So `cells batch --dry-run --format bogus` is accepted silently, unlike every other command in this change, and any throw from `getConfig(opts)` / `printDryRun(...)` now escapes the async action as a rejected promise instead of producing the `{ error: { code, message } }` envelope the rest of the file guarantees.

samples.summary: A CLI login with an unusable port silently completes a full *browser* login instead of failing, leaving the CLI to hang until timeout
samples.evidence: When `parseCliPort` returns undefined the middleware calls `next()` (line 73-77), and `GitHubAuthGuard` line 57 then falls into the `else` branch, minting a web state. The callback's web branch (`auth.controller.ts:193-197`) sets session cookies and redirects to `FRONTEND_URL`. The user is signed into the web app from a `wafflebase login` invocation while the CLI waits the full 180s and reports only `Login timed out.` with no refusal recorded.

samples.summary: `loginErrorUrl` tolerates a missing FRONTEND_URL and emits a relative redirect onto the backend origin
samples.evidence: `(this.configService.get<string>('FRONTEND_URL') ?? '')` yields `''`, so the refusal redirects to `/login?error=oauth_state` — a path that only exists on the frontend origin, giving a 404 on the backend. The success path on line 197 uses `this.configService.get('FRONTEND_URL')!`, i.e. treats the var as required; the two paths disagree about whether it can be absent.

`formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: !localOpts.raw })` only applies on the CSV branch; `sheets export doc out.json --raw` accepts the flag and does nothing with it, with no warning or error. The flag's help text says "CSV only" but nothing enforces it.

samples.summary: A grid CSV whose header row happens to be `ref,value,formula` is silently reinterpreted as a per-cell table, dropping every row and ignoring `--start`
samples.evidence: `isCellTable` only inspects the first three header names (line 106). Any user CSV with those column names routes to `buildCellMapFromTable`, whose `if (!/^[A-Z]+\d+$/.test(ref)) continue` (line 120) silently discards every row whose first column is not a cell reference, and `--start` is silently ignored. The command still exits 0, reporting `imported: 0`.

samples.summary: Any non-GET probe to the loopback port overwrites `lastRefusal`, mislabelling the eventual timeout diagnosis
samples.evidence: `refuse(res, 403, REFUSAL.notGet)` at line 284 runs before the `code`/`state` checks and unconditionally sets `lastRefusal`. A stray HEAD/OPTIONS probe (or a browser prefetch) during the 3-minute wait therefore makes `loginTimeoutMessage` blame a non-GET request even when the real problem was, e.g., a server that never echoed `state`.

finding.summary: `isCellTable`/`toCellPatch` call string methods on values the JSON import path never coerces to strings, breaking `sheets import` of an array-of-arrays JSON containing numbers
finding.evidence: `sheets-import.ts:66` does `rows = parsed as string[][]` — an *unchecked cast*; a JSON file like `[[1,2],[3,4]]` yields numbers at runtime. The new code then calls `data[0].map((h) => h.trim().toLowerCase())` (`csv-parse.ts:105`) and `text.startsWith('=')` (`csv-parse.ts:91`), both of which throw `TypeError: h.trim is not a function` / `text.startsWith is not a function`. verdict.reason: All three cited locations exist exactly as described. sheets-import.ts:66 casts `parsed as string[][]` with no runtime coercion (contrast line 71, where the array-of-objects branch coerces via `String(o[k] ?? '')`). That uncoerced array flows into isCellTable at sheets-import.ts:93, whose only guard is `data.length === 0` (csv-parse.ts:104); csv-parse.ts:105 then calls `h.trim().toLowerCase()` on each header element, throwing `TypeError: h.trim is not a function` for a JSON file like `[[1,2],[3,4]]`. The fallback path is equally exposed: buildCellMap skips only `value === ''` (csv-parse.ts:147), which a number never satisfies, so the number reaches toCellPatch and `text.startsWith('=')` at csv-parse.ts:91. buildCellMapFromTable:119 has the same exposure. I enumerated every call site of these functions; the sole production caller is sheets-import.ts:93-95, and no guard between line 66 and line 93 validates element types, so nothing makes this unreachable. formatter.ts:106-112 confirms the catch at sheets-import.ts:111 turns the TypeError into an opaque error envelope with exit code 1, aborting the whole import. This is a missing-type-guard crash on a realistic user path, squarely in the Correctness lane, and existing tests (csv-parse.test.ts:123-133) exercise only string inputs.

finding.evidence: `buildCellMapFromTable` sends `{ formula }` verbatim whenever the formula column is non-empty (line 126-127). A default export neutralizes that column to `'=SUM(B2:B100)` (`csv.ts:41`). Importing that file therefore PATCHes the cell with `f: "'=SUM(B2:B100)"` — a malformed formula stored server-side, with no error and `imported: N` reported as success. Only the docs warn to pass `--raw`; nothing in the import path detects the guard prefix or rejects it.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `formatCsv` neutralizes every field including the formula column (csv.ts:91 -> neutralizeFormula csv.ts:33-42), and export defaults to neutralizing (sheets-export.ts:61-63, only `--raw` disables it), so a default CSV export contains `'=SUM(B2:B100)` in the formula column. On import, `buildCellMapFromTable` forwards the formula column verbatim with no `=`-prefix check and no stripping of the `'` guard (csv-parse.ts:126-127); `toCellPatch`'s `startsWith('=')` test is only applied to the value/grid path (csv-parse.ts:90-91, 129, 149). sheets-import.ts:93-110 sends that patch and prints `{ imported: N }` on success. The backend performs no formula validation — `f: cellData.formula ?? existing?.f` (cells.controller.ts:168-172) stores the malformed `'=SUM(...)` string as the cell formula, overwriting any prior formula. Grep found no guard-prefix detection anywhere in the import path (only the `--raw` help text at sheets-export.ts:32 and schema/registry.ts:580). This is a reachable silent data-corruption path in the documented export→import round trip, in the correctness lane; documentation advising `--raw` is not a guard.

finding.summary: `buildCellMap` now reinterprets any grid-CSV cell whose text starts with `=` as a formula, changing existing import semantics and breaking export→import identity for literal `=`-leading text
finding.evidence: `toCellPatch(text)` returns `{ formula: text }` for anything starting with `=` and is now used by `buildCellMap` (line 149), which previously always produced `{ value }`. A cell legitimately set as text (`cells set A1 "=N/A"` stores `v='=N/A'`) exports with `value='=N/A'`, and `buildCellMapFromTable` line 129 routes it through `toCellPatch`, so the re-import converts stored text into an evaluated formula. Existing CSVs containing `=`-leading text columns silently change meaning on import.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `toCellPatch` (csv-parse.ts:90-92) maps any `=`-leading text to `{formula}`, and it is now used by both `buildCellMap` (line 149, which per the repo's own round-9 note previously always emitted `{value}`) and `buildCellMapFromTable` (line 129). The table path is a genuine logic bug: at line 128 the export's `formula` column is empty, which authoritatively means the source cell held text (`value: cell?.v`, `formula: cell?.f` at backend cells.controller.ts:62-63), yet the value is still reinterpreted as a formula. A concrete reachable corruption path exists: `cells set A1 "=N/A"` sends `{value}` (cells.ts:50,68-69) and the backend stores it in `v` (cells.controller.ts:122-123); `sheets export --raw` writes it verbatim (sheets-export.ts:63 with neutralizeFormulas:false, output/csv.ts:91); `sheets import` routes it through buildCellMapFromTable (sheets-import.ts:93-95) producing `{formula:'=N/A'}`, which the backend stores into `f` (cells.controller.ts:170-171). Text becomes an evaluated formula, so the documented `--raw` round-trip identity (sheets-export.ts:56-60) is broken and stored cell semantics are overwritten. The only mitigation, the export-side `'` prefix (output/csv.ts:33-41), is disabled on exactly the `--raw` path where the loss occurs, so it is not a guard. The behavior being tested/intentional (test/csv-parse.test.ts:113-120) does not make the information-discarding conversion correct; data-semantics overwrite is within the correctness lane.

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review: every credential in the pool (2) was retired — nothing left to fail over to

verdict.reason: The finding names no file, no line, and no code behavior. Its text is verbatim the review harness's own runtime error string, built at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:630-637 (poolExhaustedError) and thrown at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:743 and via failoverStep at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:690-693 when every Claude credential in the pool has been retired. It records that the upstream reviewer process (label "review", pool size 2) ran out of API credentials and aborted before producing a verdict — an operational failure of the review run, not a defect in repository code. No wrong condition, missing guard, async mistake, or broken invariant is asserted anywhere, so there is no described code defect present to confirm. The code that emits the message is itself coherent at those lines: exhaustion is gated on pool.isExhausted(), the error is tagged kind "pool-exhausted" with retryable=false so callers' withRetry will not back off on an unclearable condition.
